Sumeet Goel,
 Goel, J. (Oral)

Present petition has been filed under Section 482 of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
(for short 'Bnss') for grant of concession of anticipatory bail to the petitioner petitioner, in case Fir
No.14 dated 26.05.2025,, under Sections 409, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120 120-B B of the Ipc,
1860 and Sections 13(2) and 13(1)(c) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, registered at Police
Station Anti Anti-Corruption Corruption Bureau, District Rohtak.

2. On 31.07.2025, the he following order was passed:
"Notice of motion.

On the asking of the Bench, Mr. Viney Phogat, Dag Haryana accepts notice on behalf
of the petitioner and prays for time to file reply to the petition.

Till the next date of hearing, nnoo coercive steps be taken qua the petitioner."
1 of 3 CRM- CRM-M-41038- 41038-2025 2.1.

Thereafter, on 17.09.2025, the following order was passed:
"The petitioner is directed to join investigation once again within a period of one week.
Adjourned to 30.10.2025.
Interim order to continue."

3. Reiterating submissions earlier made, learned Senior counsel submits that the petitioner is a lady aged 45 years with clean antecedents, the main accused, i.e., husband of the petitioner, namely Mainpal stands arrested, two co-accused, namely, Sonu alias Sonu Kumar and Kulwant Singh alias Kulwant have been granted concession of regular bail, by this Court, vide orders dated 28.01.2026 passed in CRM- CRM-M-61124- 61124-2025 and CRM- CRM-M-60155- 60155-2025, 2025 respectively.

4. Per contra, learned State counsel (on instructions Inspector Sanjeev Kumar) has stated that the petitioner has joined investigation, but there are direct/ serious allegations against the petitioner,
the recovery of money in question is yet to be effected, and keeping in view the gravity of offence, the petitioner ought not to be extended concession of anticipatory bail.

5. Having heard learned counsel for the rival parties; especially the factum of petitioner being lady and having joined investigation and her custodial interrogation is being sought for only to recover money in question, the interim orders dated 31.07.2025 and 17.09.2025 passed by this Court are made absolute, subject to the conditions as enumerated under Section 482(2) of BNSS, 2023.
6.
Petition stands allowed, accordingly.
7. This order should not be treated as "blanket" order.
It will not be read granting petitioner indefinite protection from arrest.

It shall be 2 of 3 CRM- Suman vs State Of Haryana on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80273968/
2 CRM-M-41038- 41038-2025 confined to the FIR mentioned ibid and will not operate in respect of any other incident that involves commission of an offence.
8. Liberty is reserved in favour of State/complainant to move for cancellation/recall of this order in case the petitioner violates any condition stipulated under Section 482(2) of BNSS, 2023 or upon showing any other sufficient cause.
